newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says to auction oil terminal concessions Q3.
newsitem.headline: Peru says to auction oil terminal concessions Q3.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Friday it plans to re-launch its program to place state oil assets under the control of private firms by auctioning in the third quarter of the year concessions to operate oil terminals.
The auctions of eight concessions will start "not long after mid-year", privatization chief Jorge Izquierdo told reporters after a mining asset auction.
"It will be under a scheme of concessions. We are basically looking for operators" for the terminals, he added.
Granting concessions in the oil sector would mark a change of strategy by the government, which had previously passed its non-exploration oil assets into the private sector with direct sales.
Last November, the government put on hold its oil privatization program after the sale of a 60-percent stake in its La Pampilla refinery raised public fears of gasoline price hikes.
Izquierdo said then that the privatization board would devise auction schemes to ensure more government control over the industry.
The government has not announced a date for the sale of the country's second largest refinery, Talara, which was originally slated for the first quarter this year.
Izquierdo spoke Friday after the government sold its La Oroya metallurgic complex of refineries and smelters to Mexico's Industrias Penoles SA for $185 million.

The government's privatization program -- started in 1991 - - has so far drawn direct income of almost $7 billion and commitments from buyers to invest up to a total of almost $5 billion, according to the privatization board.

But with few major assets left to sell, the government has said it will now concentrate on granting the private sector concessions to carry out public sector infrastructure projects. The government hopes to attract $8 billion in this so-called "second phase" of the privatization program.
